summary: This script lets you interactively pick a Docker image using a fuzzy finder, then run it as a temporary container. You can optionally run it as root by pressing Ctrl-R instead of Enter, and it automatically picks the best shell available in the container.

explanations.4: This checks that both 'fzf' (a fuzzy search tool) and 'docker' are installed and available; if either is missing, the script exits early.
explanations.10: This is the start of a multi-line string that defines what information fzf will show in a preview pane — it uses docker inspect to fetch detailed metadata about each image.
explanations.22: This runs docker images to list all your images with four columns (repository:tag, ID, size, and creation date), then pipes that output to fzf so you can search and select.
explanations.23: The fzf command sets up a full-screen search interface with a reverse layout (search at bottom) and enables Ctrl-R as a special key to trigger a different behavior later.
explanations.31: The fzf output includes which key was pressed on the first line; this extracts just that first line to check if the user pressed Ctrl-R or just Enter.
explanations.32: This grabs everything after the first line of fzf output — that's the actual image row the user selected (with the repository, ID, size, and creation date).
explanations.33: From the selected image row, this extracts the second column, which is the short image ID needed to run the container.
explanations.39: If the user pressed Ctrl-R, this sets a flag to add --user root to the docker run command, making the container run as the root user instead of the default.
explanations.42: This builds a command that will start a shell inside the container, trying zsh first, then bash, then falling back to sh if neither exists.
explanations.43: This assembles the full docker run command with all the pieces (the image ID, user flag, and smart shell), then collapses any extra spaces so the command looks clean.
